prompt: Do long division by hand in a loop to find the repeating block of 1/d, using repeated remainders to detect the cycle. Complete cycleLength and cycleDigits.
explanation: Long division produces one digit per round from remainder * 10 / d, and the next remainder is remainder * 10 % d. A remainder of 0 means the expansion terminates; seeing the SAME remainder twice means the digits between those two sightings repeat forever, which is the cycle. Recording the position at which each remainder first appeared -- an int array indexed by remainder is ideal, since remainders are always below d -- turns the cycle length into a subtraction.
hints: Simulate long division: each round the next digit is remainder * 10 / d and the next remainder is remainder * 10 % d.
Remember the position at which each remainder was first seen; an int[d] filled with -1 works because every remainder is smaller than d.

Stop when the remainder hits 0 (the expansion terminates, so there is no cycle) or when you meet a remainder you have seen before -- the cycle length is the current digit count minus the position where that remainder first appeared.
